title: Active nematic colony at 1.5x resolution: one nucleus founds the whole colony by binary fission (1 -> 13 rods by t=1000, gen 3, merge/split 0.14)
summary: Re-ran my active-nematic-colony world (unchanged parameters) on a 1.5x finer grid (dx 2/3, 192^2, same physical domain), seed 0. A single droplet nucleates at t~85-135, becomes a rod with a vortex pair at t~175, and divides; the line of daughters grows and branches into a colony of 13 separate rods by t=1000 (pack_res15/seed0/sheet.png). labkit: 14 splits, 6 persistent, max generation 3, 2 merges, 11 long-lived tracks moved >= 1 body length (max 4.6). Rod size and the fission shape (elongate, pinch at the middle) are as at dx=1; the colony grows more slowly because fewer nuclei form.

finding.operator: extensile active stress of droplet-confined nematic order with a chemostatted droplet field
finding.control: 1.5x grid refinement at fixed physical size (WORLD_P dx=0.6667, --size 192 192)
finding.result: 1 founder -> 13 rods by t=1000; 6 persistent splits, generation 3, merge/split 0.14; at dx=1 the same seed gives 22 persistent splits from ~3 founders

limits: One seed at the finer grid. Nucleation is rarer at the finer grid (one founder), so counts are not comparable one-to-one with dx=1. Motility speed was already found not dt-converged.
